supportStrength.description: Evidence-to-Claim support strength. Omitted means entails for legacy claimId producers; cited means reference/context only and does not satisfy policy support.

collectedByKind.description: What kind of collector produced this item (added at schemaVersion 9): a person, a deterministic program (parser, test runner, probe), or a model. Descriptive only: the status function never reads it. `collectedBy` stays the collector's identity. Absent means not declared, never any particular kind.

inconclusive.description: Present when the attempt to collect this evidence could not run or could not reach its source (added at schemaVersion 9), as distinct from a check that ran and failed (`passing: false`). An inconclusive item MUST be `supportStrength: "cited"` and MUST NOT carry `passing`, so it satisfies no policy requirement and disputes nothing (status-function.md §Evidence partitioning).

detail.description: Free-text detail. Must contain at least one non-whitespace character, where whitespace is what the ECMAScript regular expression class \s matches (ECMA-262 WhiteSpace and LineTerminator, which include U+00A0 and U+FEFF), as JSON Schema regular expressions are defined.

passing.description: Whether the check that produced this evidence passed. Omitted when the evidence is not the output of a pass/fail check.

blocking.description: Whether a non-passing result should block (e.g. trigger disputed status under a policy conflict rule).

execution.description: How the evidence was produced: the command or tool invocation, exit code, and duration — making artifacts self-describing without requiring the producer's adapter config.

then.$comment: Inconclusive evidence carries no result and is never entailing. These two constraints are what keep it out of status derivation; removing either would let an attempt that never ran satisfy a requirement or dispute a claim.
